fields.why: The only computed contrasts are percent changes ('increased 41%, from 41.7% to 58.8%', 'increased 134%', 'decreased 2%'); year-to-year percentages such as 85.7% vs 81% are only set side by side and no percentage-point difference or shortfall from target is computed. B's 'both' rests on a side-by-side quote.

Age <15 years enters only as the denominator of the NPAFP rate indicator, so recording it as 'population' (A, per 'age recorded always') and omitting it as part of a measure definition (B) are both defensible; level 0 either way.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether an age restriction that only defines a rate's denominator (per 100,000 aged <15) counts as an age dimension with role 'population'.
